bandReport.notes: Band covers items 85-100, four per page, two per column, with no item straddling a page break. Page 18 opens with item 85 whole at the top of p18-c1 - nothing continues from page 17 (band b4, which ends at item 84), so there is no mid-item opening to report. Page 21 ends with item 100 whole at the foot of p21-c2, which is the last item of the paper; the booklet nevertheless still prints '[ P.T.O.' in the p21 footer. Column crops: all eight were usable and every item was read from its column crop, never from the whole page. The three right-column crops p18-c2, p19-c2 and p20-c2 each carry a narrow sliver of the LEFT column's right-hand edge down their far-left margin (isolated single letters such as 'e', 'y', 'r' from the neighbouring column's line ends). It is cosmetic overspill, not a slice: every item number is present at the top of its own column, no line of item text is cut, and each item's stem and its four options sit wholly inside one crop. I cross-checked all four page structures against pNN.png and the c1/c2 attribution is confirmed for all 16 items - 85,86 | 87,88 on p18; 89,90 | 91,92 on p19; 93,94 | 95,96 on p20; 97,98 | 99,100 on p21. Printed-form notes carried as per-question flags: item 88 sets its decimal with a raised/middle dot ('3.2%' printed as 3<middle dot>2%); items 92, 93 and 97 are genuine two-column grids joined by a ':' and are rendered as GFM pipe tables; item 95 is the same grid shape but prints NO column headings at all, so its pipe table carries an empty header row rather than invented headings. No duplicated option, no missing option, no garbled stem and no numbering skip was found anywhere in the band; every one of the 16 items has exactly four options (a)-(d).
